### Polar and Non-Polar Dielectrics
- **Polar Dielectrics:** Materials in which the center of mass of positive charges does not coincide with the center of mass of negative charges, possessing a permanent dipole moment (e.g., $HCl, H_2O$).
- **Non-Polar Dielectrics:** Materials in which the center of mass of positive charges coincides with the center of mass of negative charges, having zero permanent dipole moment in the absence of an electric field (e.g., $H_2, N_2, CO_2$).

### Effect of Electric Field
When an external electric field $E$ is applied, polar molecules tend to align their permanent dipoles parallel to the field direction (orientation polarization), while non-polar molecules get distorted, separating positive and negative centers to induce a dipole moment (electronic/ionic polarization).
proTip: Remember that non-polar dielectrics only acquire induced dipole moments, whereas polar ones undergo both alignment and slight stretching.
